Trend dominated, moderate ranking stability suggests a robust simple combine like median could be competitive.
test a weighted scheme with inverse_error weights, since ranking stability is moderate and we want a different kind of combination than median.
Test a simple mean combination to see if averaging outlier models improves over median given trend dominance.
The series has moderate ranking stability and a strong trend; a deterministic weighted average (dba) could exploit consistent ranking.
trend dominated with moderate ranking stability; try a trimmed mean to reduce influence of outlier models.
ranking stability is moderate and errors are correlated; a per‑horizon best‑model weighting could capture horizon‑specific strengths.
The series is trend dominated with moderate ranking stability; a forward‑selection weight that adapts to complementary errors could outperform simple inverse error.
The series is trend dominated with moderate ranking stability; a model‑specific meta‑model weighting might capture subtle cross‑series patterns not captured by simple inverse/error weights.
trend dominated, moderate ranking stability – try a tighter trimmed mean to reduce influence of worst models.
test weighted combination on the smaller correlated‑group pool4 using inverse_error weights to see if a focused weighted mean improves over median on this trend‑dominated series.
The series is trend‑dominated with moderate ranking stability; try a per‑horizon best‑model weighting on the reduced pool to capture horizon‑specific strengths.

decision.justification: Selected 'median' (an agent proposal) as the best of 12 backtested attempts, score 0.3869. Series context: trend strength 0.9569 and seasonal strength 0.0709; model ranking is moderate across windows (Kendall tau 0.353); 8 of 19 models carry independent error; relative error spread across the pool is 25.798.
